Turn scattered feedback into a reviewable set of themes.

All use cases ↗

Define the sample first

Feedback analysis is only as clear as the set being analyzed. Give Maia an authorized export or collection with the period, source, product area, and any account labels the team may use. State whether repeated messages from one customer count as separate observations or one continuing issue.

The output should begin with that scope. Twenty support tickets from one week cannot establish what the whole customer base wants. They can reveal issues worth investigating.

Keep examples attached

Ask Maia to group feedback by the underlying job or problem, not by shared words alone. Two customers may describe the same reporting difficulty using different terms. Conversely, two mentions of "export" may refer to unrelated tasks.

Each theme should link back to representative records and show how many distinct customers or conversations it contains, when those fields are available. Reviewers can then open the evidence and decide whether the grouping makes sense.

Preserve disagreement

A tidy summary can erase important differences. One user may want more automation while another wants a confirmation step. Maia should retain both views and note the conditions around them. Low-frequency feedback from a strategically important workflow should remain visible even if it does not form a large cluster.

Duplicates need context too. Several copied ticket descriptions may reflect one incident rather than independent demand. Ask Maia to identify likely duplicates and keep the original records accessible.

Move from themes to questions

The theme review can propose follow-up questions, affected workflows, and evidence gaps. It should not convert mention counts directly into roadmap priority. Product managers still weigh customer impact, strategy, effort, risk, and the quality of the sample.

Post the review in the relevant Slack channel so support, success, and product owners can correct the interpretation. Maia can update the grouping after they identify a duplicate account or a misread example.

Try a bounded review

Start with one month of feedback for a single product area. Remove fields the review does not need, confirm who may see the records, and ask Maia for no more than a practical set of themes. Manually inspect examples from every group. This reveals whether the labels help the team make a decision.

Questions from product teams

Can Maia rank feature requests?

It can summarize supplied evidence and apply criteria you provide. The product team should choose priority after considering factors that feedback volume alone does not capture.

How are minority views handled?

Ask for a separate section covering conflicting or low-frequency observations. This keeps useful edge cases from disappearing into the dominant theme.

What about sensitive feedback?

Use only records authorized for the channel and remove unnecessary personal details. Keep restricted feedback in an audience with matching access.
